direct_answer:
Solvay integrates sustainability-related performance into its incentive schemes through a dedicated “sustainability ambition” pillar used across multiple plans. Solvay operates different incentive schemes for different employee groups: (i) a Short-term Incentive (STI) scheme for Management, Senior Management and Executives, (ii) a Global Profit Sharing scheme for non-management employees, and (iii) a Long-term Incentive (LTI) scheme for Senior Management and Executives; these schemes are structured around two or three performance pillars: financial performance, the Company’s sustainability ambition, and (for STI) individual contribution [Source 1].

Performance is assessed against specific sustainability-related targets in the STI and Global Profit Sharing schemes under the sustainability pillar; for STI in 2024 these targets include: Scope 1&2 GHG emissions (7,170 kT CO2 eq, based on financial perimeter), safety (recordable injuries: 40), and diversity (% women in mid and senior management: 27.3) [Source 1]. Climate-related considerations are also explicitly factored into remuneration via GHG emission reduction targets set in both STI and LTI for the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and Senior Management; for general management (except Commercial/Sales) GHG emission reduction is part of STI; and GHG emission reduction is reflected in the profit sharing plan for non-management employees [Source 2].

Sustainability-related performance metrics are included in Solvay’s Group remuneration policies (including the Executive Remuneration Policy, STI, LTI and Global Profit Sharing agreement) under the sustainability pillar [Source 1]. The proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets is disclosed as 15% of STI for all management levels, 15% of Global Profit Sharing for non-management levels, and 20% of LTI for all executives [Source 1].

The approval/update level for incentive scheme terms is described through the target-setting and approval process: for STI, KPIs are defined in line with budget/objectives, reviewed by the Global Incentive Committee (recommendation to ELT), then a final recommendation goes to the Compensation Committee (review/approval for recommendation to the Board), and the Board of Directors gives final approval [Source 7]. A similar approval chain (Global Incentive Committee, ELT, Compensation Committee, Board of Directors) applies to the LTI, which is set up annually for a three-year performance period [Source 7].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide (a) key characteristics of the incentive schemes (STI, LTI, Global Profit Sharing; performance pillars) [Source 1], (b) specific sustainability targets/metrics used (GHG Scope 1&2, safety, diversity; plus GHG reduction embedded across schemes) [Sources 1, 2], (c) confirmation that sustainability metrics are included in remuneration policies under a sustainability pillar [Source 1], (d) proportions of variable remuneration linked to sustainability targets (15% STI, 15% profit sharing, 20% LTI) [Source 1], and (e) the governance level approving targets/terms (Global Incentive Committee → ELT → Compensation Committee → Board of Directors) [Source 7]. However, evidence is insufficient to fully address ESRS 2 GOV-3 specifically for members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies because the passages do not explicitly state how sustainability metrics apply to the Board of Directors’ own remuneration (and Solvay states it has no supervisory board) [Source 3].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit statement of whether and how sustainability-related performance is integrated into the remuneration/incentives of the Board of Directors (administrative body) itself; the provided text focuses on employee/management/executive schemes and approval by the Board rather than Board member pay design [Sources 1, 7].

Clarification of sustainability-linked remuneration arrangements (if any) for supervisory bodies; Solvay states it does not have a supervisory board, but the disclosure does not explicitly map this to GOV-3 scope [Source 3].

For the LTI: the specific sustainability target level(s) and actual performance/achievement are not provided in the passages (it says LTI targets/achievements will be disclosed at end of performance period) [Source 1].
For Global Profit Sharing: the specific sustainability target(s) and threshold(s) beyond the statement that payout starts once the target is reached are not detailed in the passages [Source 1].
key_findings: Incentive schemes include a sustainability pillar alongside financial performance (and individual contribution for STI) [Source 1].
STI 2024 sustainability targets include Scope 1&2 GHG emissions, safety (recordable injuries), and diversity (% women in mid & senior management) [Source 1].

GHG emission reduction targets are embedded across STI and LTI for ELT and Senior Management, included in STI for general management (except Commercial/Sales), and reflected in profit sharing for non-management employees [Source 2].
Sustainability-linked weighting: 15% of STI (all management levels), 15% of Global Profit Sharing (non-management), 20% of LTI (all executives) [Source 1].
Approval governance: Global Incentive Committee and ELT recommendations, Compensation Committee review/approval, and final approval by the Board of Directors for STI and LTI [Source 7].
